text: The following question stood in the name of Ms Gho Sze Kee – 78 To ask the Minister for Education whether schools are resourced and equipped to (i) deal with any possible negative impact of posting group (PG) banding and (ii) promote inclusivity, interaction and friendships across different PGs in the same class.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
text: This approach gives students more opportunities than under the previous streaming system to interact with and to learn with classmates with different strengths and interests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Outside the formal curriculum, there are other group settings, such as co-curricular activities (CCAs) and Values-in-Action projects, for our students to interact with peers within and across schools.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: First, whether there are any specific guidance or professional developments to teachers managing a mixed PG classroom.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Specifically, I ask this because prior to mixed PG classroom, teachers would teach a class with similar profile, specifically in subjects like Character and Citizenship Education and Design and Technology.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Given a mixed PG classroom now, teachers then would have to engage in a classroom with wider student profiles.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Second, if there is professional development or guidance given, what is the current take-up rate and training that teachers have gone through and have we gotten any feedback from teachers about the usefulness of such training in helping them to manage a mixed PG classroom with students of different learning profiles?

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: I will try and answer both questions in just one answer.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Every student, every child and therefore every mixed form class will be unique.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We are also observing how many of our teachers are coming up and developing their own approaches in managing more of these mixed form classes.
